sections.text_helper: Section 36.7.4 "Global frequency response" in chapter 36 (Audio digital filter (ADF)), RM0486 Rev 4, page 1756.
sections.section_content:
Figure381 shows the global frequency response for a 16 kHz audio signal with a digital
microphone working at 1.024 MHz. The filter configuration is the following:
• CIC order 4 or 5, with a decimation ratio of 16
• RSFLT enabled, with a decimation ratio of 4
• HPF enabled with a cut-off frequency of 40 Hz
Figure382 shows the theoretical frequency response using a CIC4 and a CIC5.
[Figure 382. Global frequency response]
Figure383 shows the in-band ripple for a 16 kHz audio signal with a digital microphone
working at 1.024 MHz. The filter configuration is the following:
• CIC order 4 or 5, with a decimation ratio of 16
• RSFLT enabled, with a decimation ratio of 4
• HPF enabled with a cut-off frequency of 20 Hz
The resulting in-band ripple is ± 0.41 dB for CIC5, and ± 0.45 dB for CIC4.
The - 3 dB cut-off frequency is 7061 Hz.
[Figure 383. Detailed frequency response]
